question: Who gave the term 'homo sapiens'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**C. Linnaeus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Carl Linnaeus** (also known as Carl von Linné) was a Swedish botanist, zoologist, and physician who formalized the modern system of naming organisms called **binomial nomenclature**.
 
• Linnaeus is often referred to as the **"father of modern taxonomy"**.
 
• He introduced the term **"Homo sapiens"** in his work *Systema Naturae* in 1758, which is used to classify human beings.
 
• Linnaeus's classification system laid the foundation for the **Linnaean taxonomy**, which is still in use today with modifications and advancements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taxonomy**

 
 
• Taxonomy is the science of naming, defining, and classifying organisms into groups based on shared characteristics.
 
• It involves a hierarchical system of classification, starting from broader categories like Domain and Kingdom down to specific categories like Genus and Species.
 
• Carl Linnaeus's system of binomial nomenclature assigns each organism a two-part Latin name: the genus name and the species name (e.g., Homo sapiens).
 
• This system helps in accurately identifying and communicating about different species across the world.
 
 
 
• **Binomial Nomenclature**
 
 
• Binomial nomenclature is a formal system of naming species of living things by giving each a name composed of two parts.
 
• The first part of the name indicates the genus to which the species belongs, and the second part identifies the species within the genus.
 
• This method of naming organisms ensures that each has a unique and universally accepted name.
 
• Linnaeus standardized this system, making it easier to catalog and study the vast diversity of life on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Systema Naturae**
 
 
• *Systema Naturae* is one of the major works of Carl Linnaeus, first published in 1735.
 
• In this work, Linnaeus introduced his method for classifying and naming organisms.
 
• The 10th edition of *Systema Naturae*, published in 1758, is considered the starting point of zoological nomenclature.
 
• This publication marked a significant advancement in the field of biology and laid the groundwork for modern biological classification.
